title: Romualdez appeals 90-day suspension order
summary: Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has asked the Sandiganbayan to reconsider its order imposing a 90-day suspension against him as he faces a P7.4-billion plunder case in connection with alleged kickbacks…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has asked the Sandiganbayan to reconsider its order imposing a 90-day suspension against him as he faces a P7.4-billion plunder case in connection with alleged kickbacks from government infrastructure projects.
In his motion for reconsideration, the former speaker argued that some issues have yet to be resolved, including the validity of the charge filed against him.

Romualdez said the court erred in finding the charge against him valid, considering that the prosecution did not identify a main plunderer, even if a 2016 Supreme Court ruling on the Arroyo v. People case requires that such should be identified when a case is filed against several individuals.

The Leyte lawmaker pointed out that the charges accused him and former Ako Bicol party-list representative Zaldy Co of receiving money and taking undue advantage of their official positions to unjustly enrich themselves.

“It does not state which of the two is the main plunderer. Neither does it state how much of the aggregate P7.4 billion each of them supposedly amassed. This should be resolved before the Information may serve as the basis for preventive suspension,” he said.

He also questioned the court’s finding that the acts attributable to him, his degree of participation where he supposedly gained kickbacks or commissions, are matters to be threshed out during the trial, saying whether those acts have been sufficiently alleged is a question concerning the charge itself.

Romualdez’s co-accused in the P7.4-billion plunder case include former House appropriations chairpman Co, Romualdez’s personal assistant Joselyn Sereño and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp.
